ai.title: New AI “copilot” helps engineers design better structures

" The use of algorithms to design structures has led to new parts optimized for ultralight aircraft, high-bandwidth antennas, and F1 racing cars. But the best algorithmic design techniques still require lots of computation and time: Users only see the final design after it’s complete, after which they often must start the design process all over again to make changes. That process also makes it harder to trust that the final designs are structurally sound. MIT researchers are making algorithmic designs more collaborative with a system that acts like an AI copilot.

sec.title: The School Bomb Threats Came From Accounts Already in Stolen Data
sec.brief: S. 7 million people On 11 November, bomb-threat emails hit schools across Europe. ANSA, citing the Education Ministry, reported that about 6,000 Italian schools received them. Some evacuated, others kept teaching after talking to police, so the recipient count tells you nothing about how many buildings emptied. The emails were signed “Mikhail Andropov” and threatened pupils and school staff. They also mentioned a bomb targeting the prime minister. However, these names and claims came from the sender and do not confirm who was behind the threats. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said that searches found no bombs. She described the emails as an attempt to spread fear and chaos, adding that anonymous messages would not change the school calendar.
